verdict: key consistent: 90 signs = 90 letters with the margin column read where it belongs (bottom to top, inserted after فه on 32r l.3) and الى ورده as written, 78/79 repeated occurrences (98.7%; skeleton 100%); the stacked-ε sign writes ن (اسرني) and ب (بي), one skeleton; ب, ي and م have two shapes each.
notes: Text as enciphered: قد قد قد حبيبي حبل صبري كسر وسلسل الريق سلسل اذ اسرني اسر ولولو الثغر بسامه حصر بي حصر فهل سبيل الى ورد[ه] وضم الخصر. The clear text on 32r l.12 writes الى and ورده run together (الىورده), which the record read الورده; the cipher has ا ل ي | و ر د (eight letters for the record's six). Against the record's wording: 90 signs vs 88 letters.

Order of the margin column, established from the cipher: the 11 signs in the outer margin of 32r are written so that they stand upright when the page is turned a quarter right, i.e. they read from the bottom of the column to the top. They give ل سبيل الى ورد + a sign cut by the trim (ه): the omitted middle of the second verse, to be read after the فه of فهل on 32r l.3; the last two signs of l.3 (و ض) and l.4 (م الخصر) follow. The record placed the column after l.4; read there, the text does not fit (l.4 ends الخصر, the last word).

No dividers, as the compiler says (bi-ghayr fawasil). Counts by eye: 31v l.11 12 (the dot on l.11 is a speck), l.12 12, l.13 13; 32r l.1 12, l.2 11, l.3 12, margin 11 + 1 cut, l.4 6 = 90 (record 90 with the speck).
The two '//' strokes the record thought might be word marks: one is م in بسامه, and the crossed one (≠) is م in وضم at the head of l.4.
